Repositories, images and the stack that actually runs
The only deployment view in this pack, scoped to the Legal Knowledge Database: five services, one Docker Compose environment on a lab host, and four stores behind a single-writer
rule. No production deployment is claimed anywhere.

g.text: Four of these are mine end to end: the preprocessor, the loader, the health service and the
dashboard. The entity producer existed before legal ingestion and I extended it for EU sources.
The dashboard owning nothing is a design position, not an omission. It ships with no database,
queue or object-store client at all, so there is no code path by which the operator surface could
write the corpus it reports on.
local-env is the repository that makes the others runnable: the Compose files, the service YAML
It is the answer to “where does the environment live” — the environment is itself a versioned
repository rather than a document describing one.
Each service image is built by CI and run from Docker Compose on a lab host. There is no
production deployment and none is claimed.

g.text: the failure that looked like success
Supersedes ADR-003. The package is installed editable and a boot-time check runs, so a
drifted container fails at startup instead of serving a route table nobody expected.

g.text: WHY THERE IS NO INGEST ENDPOINT
Ingestion has no REST trigger. First ingest, re-ingest and replay are the same code path, so the recovery path is exercised daily rather than on the day it is needed.

svg.text: THE SINGLE-WRITER RULE · ONE ANSWER TO “WHICH SERVICE WROTE THIS?”

g.text: HOW THE RULE WAS ARRIVED AT
The rule was arrived at by removing a violation, not by agreeing to one. An earlier loader deleted canonical rows and
could never have worked: currency_observations references laws with ON DELETE RESTRICT and is append-only, so
the delete was refused every time — after Qdrant and Neo4j had already been cleared and committed.
The resolution was to delete the code path, not to relax the constraint. One flag-gated purge path survives in the
loader, recorded as debt; nothing calls it.
A permanently unprocessable law is redelivered for ever and blocks its partition until a
human intervenes. The document pipeline has a DLQ; the legal one does not.

Nothing in the running stack scrapes or alerts.

g.text: WHAT THIS DIAGRAM DOES AND DOES NOT CLAIM

Nothing here is a production topology. The stack runs from Docker Compose with CI-built images on a lab host, which is why the ports are host ports and why the loader is the only service publishing a range rather than a single one.

Every port, language and ownership claim on this page is read from the service inventory and the single-writer table in docs/architecture/architecture-notes.md. Where a store is written by two services, both rows appear — the rule is one writer per concern, not one writer per database.

A dash in the repository column means the repository name is not published anywhere in this portfolio — not that the service has no repository. The entity producer is in that position, and guessing a plausible name for it would have put an invented identifier in a column set in mono, which in this pack means
